solutions.check: bars rebuilt from the blog's numbered answers (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Deviously help grand trickery involving energy and venting humour?

indicators.note: doing something deviously means taking a crooked route, so these letters go in a twisted order

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
G is the slang abbreviation for a grand, a thousand

indicators.note: something involving another wraps it up inside itself

parts.note: conjuring is trickery
go means energy or drive

explanation.surface: Someone cunningly helping a grand con trick that takes plenty of energy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Humour' is the old medical sense: phlegm was one of the four bodily humours, so venting it is the job of this kind of remedy.
explanation.definitionFit: A phlegmagogic medicine expels phlegm, one of the four humours of old physiology, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Ah gosh! Rapper garbled cursive sequence

indicators.note: a garbled message has its parts mixed up, so the preceding words are scrambled

parts.note: all twelve letters of the exclamation and the performer

explanation.surface: Someone gasps as a rapper mangles a run of joined-up handwriting.
explanation.definitionFit: A phraseograph is a shorthand symbol standing for a whole phrase, written as one flowing joined-up character.

clue.text: Moth took off in joint

indicators.note: off as in gone bad or out of order, so the word is rearranged
one thing sitting in another is placed inside it

parts.note: the hip is a joint of the body
the word rearranged

explanation.surface: A moth flew off from inside a joint of meat or a bar.
explanation.definitionFit: A hooktip is a moth of the family Drepanidae, named for its hooked wingtips.

clue.text: Droop on fringes of university dance

indicators.note: something on the fringes of another surrounds it on both sides

parts.note: to lop is to hang down limply
standard abbreviation

explanation.surface: Someone sagging at the edge of a university ball.
explanation.definitionFit: Loup is the Scots verb to leap or jump, so to caper about in dancing.

clue.text: Like wine making one merry dipped into regularly by distinguished don

indicators.note: the word is entered at evenly spaced points, one letter at a time, rather than in one lump

parts.note: gay in its old sense of merry, cheerful
RP is Regius Professor, a top-ranking university chair

explanation.surface: A tipsy-making wine that an eminent academic keeps sipping at.
explanation.walkthrough: R and P go in separately, one after each of the first two letters of GAY. A Regius Professor holds a royally founded chair at an old British university.
explanation.definitionFit: Grapy means tasting or smelling of grapes, which is what wine is made from.

clue.text: Radar system creating endless work — terribly solemn about it

indicators.note: lying about something surrounds it
something done terribly is done badly, so the letters are thrown about

parts.note: the word to be rearranged

indicators.note: without an end, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: Latin for a work, especially of music

explanation.surface: A radar programme producing never-ending, dreadfully serious work.
explanation.definitionFit: Monopulse is a radar technique that fixes a target's direction from a single pulse.

clue.text: Class benders (not classically proper!)

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a biological category ranking above species
second meaning: a plural of Latin genu, knee, which is a thing that bends

explanation.walkthrough: Knees are 'benders'; the Latin word for knee is genu, and the parenthesis admits that the correct Latin plural is genua, not this English-style one.
explanation.definitionFit: In biological taxonomy a genus is a classification grouping related species together.

clue.text: Outcry once dress comes into contact with grease

parts.note: garb is clothing
oil is a lubricating grease

explanation.surface: Uproar from the past when a gown gets smeared with grease.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Once' marks the definition as obsolete English.
explanation.definitionFit: Garboil is an archaic word for tumult or commotion, as used by Shakespeare.

clue.text: Mild oath senior officer produces having lost pipe outside?

indicators.note: having lost something means it has been taken away
outside says the lost word's letters come from both ends, front and back, leaving the middle

parts.note: an army rank above colonel
a brier (briar) is a tobacco pipe made from heath root; its letters sit at the start and end of the officer

explanation.surface: A senior officer swears mildly when he loses his pipe.
explanation.walkthrough: A brier (briar) pipe is carved from the root of the tree heath, a long-standing crossword favourite.
explanation.definitionFit: Igad is an old-fashioned minced oath, a softened form of 'by God'.

clue.text: Meeting-place, special, to study e.g. Playboy feature? (12, two words)

parts.note: a centre is a place where people gather
standard abbreviation
to read a subject is to study it

explanation.surface: A special meeting-place for poring over a men's magazine.
explanation.definitionFit: A centrespread is the pair of facing middle pages of a magazine, famously the pin-up in Playboy.

clue.text: Nasty Scot in Glasgow we found among personnel

indicators.note: something found among others is placed in their midst

parts.note: Human Resources, the personnel department
oo is a Scots form of 'we'

explanation.surface: A disagreeable Scotsman turns up among the staff in Glasgow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nasty' is a noun here: an unpleasant person.
explanation.definitionFit: Hoor, a Scots variant of whore, is used in Scotland for a difficult or unpleasant person or thing.

clue.text: Excess reporting? Cut initial chapter

indicators.note: cutting the initial removes the opening letter

parts.note: news coverage is reporting
standard abbreviation, here the letter to be removed

explanation.surface: Too much journalism? Then trim the first chapter.
explanation.definitionFit: An overage is a surplus, an amount over what is needed or expected.

clue.text: Rising like a bird that exercises a turn so

indicators.note: exercising works something over, so the following letters are put through their paces into a new order

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A bird taking off that goes through a turn like so.
explanation.definitionFit: In heraldry, rousant describes a bird shown with wings raised as if about to take flight.

clue.text: Bits of breakfast roughage adding nourishment

definitions.text: Bits of breakfast roughage adding nourishment

indicators.note: small bits taken from each word, namely their opening letters

parts.note: the opening letters of the four words

explanation.surface: Fibre in a morning meal that adds nutritional value.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the wordplay and the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Bran, the husks of cereal grain, is the classic fibre added to breakfast cereals.

clue.text: Extract from pasture dock for nettle rash

indicators.note: an extract is a piece pulled out of a longer text, so the letters lie within the next words

parts.note: the run of letters spanning the two words

explanation.surface: A herbal remedy from a meadow plant, dock, to soothe nettle stings.
explanation.walkthrough: Dock leaves are the traditional British rub for nettle stings, which makes the surface very natural.
explanation.definitionFit: Uredo is an old medical term for urticaria, the itchy skin eruption also called hives or nettle rash.

clue.text: Appearing when option's selected, champers at an end

parts.note: pop is fizzy wine, as is champers (champagne)
time's up means it is at an end

explanation.surface: The champagne runs out just as someone makes their choice.
explanation.definitionFit: A pop-up menu or window is one that springs into view when the user clicks or chooses something.

clue.text: Press lied freely displaying hubris? Far from it

indicators.note: letters arranged freely are not bound to their original order

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Newspapers told lies with abandon, showing arrogance... or not.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Far from it' reverses the preceding phrase, so the definition means the opposite of showing hubris.
explanation.definitionFit: Hubris is overweening pride; to lack any pride at all is the opposite of that arrogance.

clue.text: Plot ryots worked

indicators.note: worked as in kneaded or shaped, so the letters are reformed

parts.note: ryots are Indian peasant farmers; the word is rearranged

explanation.surface: Indian peasants laboured on a patch of land.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plot' suggests a piece of farmland in the surface; it is the storyline of a narrative.
explanation.definitionFit: The plot of a book or film is its story, the sequence of events it narrates.

clue.text: Singer's first substandard track

indicators.note: first picks out only the opening letter of the word before

parts.note: the initial of the word
poor quality is below standard

explanation.surface: A vocalist's debut song is a weak recording.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Track' wants to be a song on a record; here it is the trail an animal leaves.
explanation.definitionFit: Spoor is the track, scent or droppings by which a hunter follows an animal.

clue.text: Damned old and cold cramped houses

indicators.note: something that houses another holds it inside

parts.note: a poky room is small and cramped
standard abbreviation, as on a tap

explanation.surface: Grim, ancient, chilly, cramped houses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old' belongs to the definition, marking the sense as obsolete.
explanation.definitionFit: Pocky, literally pox-ridden, was formerly used as an intensifier meaning cursed or confounded.

clue.text: Stewed fruit with a dash of lemon in? It was intriguing

indicators.note: a thing in another is placed inside it

parts.note: a compote or compot is fruit stewed in syrup
a dash is a tiny amount, the initial letter

explanation.surface: A fruit compote with a squeeze of lemon was interesting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Intriguing' means plotting, not fascinating; 'was' marks the noun as archaic.
explanation.definitionFit: Complot is an old word for a conspiracy, a plot hatched by intriguers working together.

clue.text: Balance is shown following ball in French team

indicators.note: one thing in another is placed inside it

parts.note: équipe is French for team

indicators.note: coming after, so one piece is placed behind the other

parts.note: a ball is round like the letter
taken as written

explanation.surface: Poise is displayed after the ball reaches a French side.
explanation.definitionFit: Equipoise is a state of equal balance or equilibrium between forces.

clue.text: Shift is taken up and nearly spoilt

indicators.note: in a down clue, taken up means read from bottom to top
nearly means not quite all, so the last letter goes

parts.note: the word turned around
marred means damaged, spoilt

explanation.surface: A change of position is accepted and almost ruined.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shift' looks like a change or a work period; it is the old name for a woman's loose dress.
explanation.definitionFit: A simarre (simar) is a woman's loose robe or gown, the same kind of garment as a shift.

clue.text: Poodle treated by (US) vet producing type of liniment

indicators.note: a dog treated by a vet is worked on, so the word is reworked

parts.note: the dog's letters rearranged
doc is American slang for a doctor, here an animal doctor

explanation.surface: A poodle seen by an American vet is rubbed with a medicinal ointment.
explanation.definitionFit: Opodeldoc is an old soap-and-camphor liniment rubbed on for sprains and aches.

clue.text: Historical assembly learnt about them

indicators.note: one thing about another goes round it

parts.note: to get something is to understand or learn it
'em is the colloquial short form

explanation.surface: A history meeting found out about them.
explanation.definitionFit: A gemot was an Anglo-Saxon public meeting or court, an assembly of freemen.

clue.text: Blast of air, tornado with no hush inside

indicators.note: with no means without, so letters are removed
inside says the removed letters come from the middle of the word, not its ends

parts.note: an American name for a tornado
st! is an interjection calling for silence

explanation.surface: A gust from a whirlwind with silence at its heart.
explanation.walkthrough: Strictly a twier is the nozzle through which a furnace blast passes, not the blast itself, so the definition stretches a little.
explanation.definitionFit: A twier or tuyère is the pipe that delivers a blast of air into a furnace or forge.

clue.text: Spare mobile's thrown into waste container often

indicators.note: something thrown into a receptacle ends up inside it

parts.note: a skip is a large open bin for rubbish
M stands for mobile, as in m-banking or m-commerce

explanation.surface: A spare mobile phone is often chucked in the skip.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a skip is a big open metal bin hired for building rubbish.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb, spare in the sense of be sparing or stingy matches skimp, to economise too much.

clue.text: Prop displaying bulge, routine with stone put on

indicators.note: in a down answer, putting one piece on another sets it above, so it comes first

parts.note: st is the abbreviation for stone, the British weight of 14 lb
a rut is a dull fixed routine

explanation.surface: A support shows a swelling, given a regular stone weight placed on top.
explanation.walkthrough: A strut is a structural prop, and strut also once meant to swell or bulge, so the definition covers both.
explanation.definitionFit: A strut is a brace or support in a framework; as a verb it once meant to protrude or swell.

clue.text: International practice formerly sanctioned by law

parts.note: standard abbreviation
ure is an obsolete word for use or practice

explanation.surface: A worldwide custom once given legal approval.
explanation.definitionFit: Iure is Latin 'by right or law', as in de iure, the variant spelling of de jure.

clue.text: What makes society wither and die in some parts

parts.note: standard abbreviation
welt is a dialect verb meaning to wither or fade

explanation.surface: Asks what causes a community to shrivel and perish in certain regions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In some parts' marks the definition as dialect.
explanation.definitionFit: Swelt is a dialect word meaning to faint or perish, especially from heat.

clue.text: Twain-like, showing what's universal in boy's upbringing

indicators.note: bringing up, in a down answer, means reading from the bottom upwards
one thing in another sits inside it

parts.note: a boy is a lad, turned around
U is the film certificate meaning universal

explanation.surface: Something resembling Mark Twain, shown by what is common to every boy's raising.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Twain' wants to be Mark Twain; it is the old word for two.
explanation.definitionFit: Twain means two, so something twain-like is double, having two parts.

clue.text: Hall, type of expansion university welcomed

indicators.note: a guest welcomed in is taken inside

parts.note: an ala is a wing or winglike expansion in botany and anatomy
standard abbreviation

explanation.surface: A hall where some kind of growth was welcomed by a university.
explanation.definitionFit: Aula is a large hall, especially a university assembly hall in Germany or Scandinavia.

clue.text: Feature of green belt behind schedule, not the first? About right

indicators.note: lying about something surrounds it
not the first says the opening letter is left out

parts.note: overdue means late
standard abbreviation

explanation.surface: Development in the protected countryside running late, except for the first part, is about right.
explanation.walkthrough: A green belt is the protected ring of countryside round a British town where building is restricted.
explanation.definitionFit: Verdure is lush green vegetation, the very thing that makes a green belt green.

clue.text: Blind cave-dweller erupts furiously, pierced by Odysseus initially

indicators.note: acting furiously means flying about wildly, so the letters are scattered

parts.note: the word to be rearranged

indicators.note: initially means only the first letter is wanted

parts.note: the hero's initial

explanation.surface: The blind Cyclops in his cave bursts out in rage, stabbed by Odysseus.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface evokes Polyphemus, but the cave-dweller is an amphibian; the O joins the anagram fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Proteus is the genus of the olm, a blind salamander living in underground caves of the Balkans.

clue.text: It carries significance for Sikhs, knocking back strong drink

indicators.note: knocking back suggests going backwards, so the word is read in the other direction

parts.note: arak is a strong spirit distilled in the Middle East and Asia

explanation.surface: Something of religious importance to Sikhs is drinking hard liquor.
explanation.definitionFit: The kara, a steel bangle, is one of the five Ks that baptised Sikhs wear as articles of faith.

clue.text: The old trees they varied with flower parts of differing length

definitions.text: with flower parts of differing length

indicators.note: something varied has been changed about, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the twelve letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Ancient trees that differed in having flowers with uneven parts.
explanation.walkthrough: The opening 'The' plays no part in the wordplay; it only smooths the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Heterostyled plants such as primroses have flowers whose styles differ in length from plant to plant.
